S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-accepted protocol and representative samples. The maximum allowed failure rate is 5%. The regulator shall determine whether interim sales restrictions are necessary based on the risk and adequacy of corrective measures; further sales shall be restricted where the regulator finds an imminent or unresolved serious risk.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-accepted protocol and representative samples. The maximum allowed failure rate is 5%. A model exceeding that limit requires prompt regulator notification, a time-bound corrective-action plan, and retesting. The regulator shall determine whether interim sales restrictions are necessary based on the risk and adequacy of corrective measures; further sales shall be restricted where the regulator finds an imminent or unresolved serious risk. Per-model results, including failure rates and test protocols, shall be provided to regulators and to customers who buy that model in a clear safety summary. Results shall not be published to the general public.

S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units placed on the market from 24 months after adoption shall support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers shall provide compatible retrofit capability or an equivalent safe mitigation within 6 years, prioritizing units with known safety concerns. Customers shall receive advance notice and installation instructions; any shut-off must not compromise essential emergency functions.

S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units placed on the market from 36 months after adoption shall include built-in fire suppression meeting applicable safety requirements. Manufacturers shall provide customers with instructions on system operation, inspection, and maintenance.

parameters.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and cooperate in a regulator-supervised recall assessment. The regulator shall require a recall when the threshold is exceeded, unless it determines that a time-bound corrective action provides an equally protective remedy; an equivalent serious risk independently warrants a recall.

The regulator shall require a recall when the threshold is exceeded, unless it determines that a time-bound corrective action provides an equally protective remedy; an equivalent serious risk independently warrants a recall.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall provide customers clear safety notices about material risks, relevant test results for their model, recommended precautions, and corrective actions, promptly when a material safety risk is identified and whenever findings materially change. When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers and cooperate in a regulator-supervised recall assessment. The regulator shall require a recall when the threshold is exceeded, unless it determines that a time-bound corrective action provides an equally protective remedy; an equivalent serious risk independently warrants a recall. A recall means prompt customer notification and an effective repair, replacement, refund, or safe-use/shutdown remedy, and does not by itself require a permanent sales ban. Regulators shall be notified of the trigger, assessment, and recall or corrective actions.

judge_section_notes: S2 has no automatic sales stop: the regulator decides on restrictions, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10 at 6.2% failure. S3 sets the new-unit shut-off deadline at 24 months (beyond the 12-month acceptable range) and the retrofit at 6 years, which fits Northwind's red line and its 38% installed-base figure. S4 (36 months) meets Halcyon's red line, and S5 makes an 8-per-100k recall mandatory, which Ember 8 at 9.9 would trigger, though recall is not a sales ban. The S5 corrective-action alternative is described as time-bound but has no stated end, so its bounded/open status is ambiguous.
